terms.comment: Particular as against any at all: certīs diēbus, on particular days; “this particular …” is often ipse: hōc ipsō diē.

evidence: Sen. Ep. 7.1: quid tibi vītandum praecipuē exīstimēs quaeris? turbam
Hor. Ep. 1.1.108: praecipuē sānus, nisi cum pītuīta molesta est

terms.grammar: adverb; most often with cum or sī
terms.comment: Traupman gives potissimum, “above all”, for “in particular” (p. 356).

terms.gloss: of a part, partial; in logic, particular
terms.comment: Traupman’s word for “particular”, but post-classical and a term of logic (prōpositiōnēs particulārēs, opposed to universal ones); certus and praecipuus say it classically.

phrases.latin: quid tibi vītandum praecipuē exīstimēs quaeris? turbam
phrases.english: you ask what I think you should avoid in particular? Crowds
it is kindness, in particular, that wins hearts

phrases.latin: temporibus certīs mātūram rūsticus ūvam dēligit
phrases.english: at particular times the farmer picks the ripe grapes

sources: Lewis & Short: certus · Lewis & Short: praecipuus (praecipuē) · Lewis & Short: praesertim · Lewis & Short: particularis
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 356.
